name: Grid
description: A composite widget container enabling users to navigate information or interactive elements using directional keys, serving as either a data grid or layout grid.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus one cell to the right
Moves focus one cell to the left
Moves focus down an author-determined number of rows
Moves focus up an author-determined number of rows
Moves focus to the first cell in the current row
Moves focus to the last cell in the current row
Moves focus to the first cell in the first row
Moves focus to the last cell in the last row
Places focus in editable input field or first widget within cell
Places focus in input field; subsequent F2 restores grid navigation
Restores grid navigation; may undo edits

required_attributes.description: Provides accessible name for the grid

optional_attributes.description: Total columns when some are hidden
Total rows when some are hidden

notes: role='grid' is for a table you NAVIGATE and INTERACT with — a spreadsheet, an editable data grid. A read-only data table is patterns/table.md and needs none of this.
Adding role='grid' to a static table is a downgrade: it switches screen readers into application mode and forces users to learn arrow navigation for content they could already read normally.
Build it on a real <table> with <th scope>. role='grid' on <table> keeps the header associations (RAWeb 5.6, 5.7) and adds the interaction model.
One Tab stop, roving tabindex on cells: tabindex='0' on the focused cell, '-1' on all others.
Because arrows are captured, Tab is the ONLY way out — never intercept it (RAWeb 12.9).
A cell containing an interactive control needs a mode switch: Enter to enter the cell and interact, Escape to return to grid navigation. Otherwise arrow keys inside a text input fight the grid.
aria-colcount/aria-rowcount only when the DOM does not hold every row (virtualisation). Otherwise the browser counts.
native_element: <table> — if it is not interactive, you want patterns/table.md, not this

raweb_criteria.reason: grid/row/gridcell roles and any selection state must be exposed.
Arrow keys must move between cells in two dimensions.
The focused cell must be visibly indicated.
Roving tabindex makes the whole grid one Tab stop.
Tab must escape the grid — this pattern captures arrows, so Tab is the only way out.
If built on a <table>, headers must still be declared with <th> and scope.
Cells must remain associated with their headers.
